titleEn: I Only Put a Little In

pages.text: In winter, birds had no food. Grandpa put Nono in charge of the feeder.
Nono wanted to fill it. Then many birds would come.
He scooped one handful of feed from a sack. It barely covered the bottom.
Singing came from the alley. Nono hopped onto the feed sack and sang along.
While he sang, sparrows pecked up everything. The feeder was already empty.
Two sparrows peered into the empty feeder. Nobody sat on the branch.
Snow fell again. Only snow piled in the empty feeder.
Grandpa Badger said, "Once, I went to bed after putting in just one handful too. Not a bird came in the morning."
Nono scooped feed in, then more. It filled right to overflowing.
Birds fluttered in. The branch filled with birds.
